p: The Trafford Centre and the wider Trafford City area are packed with family attractions, so a round of golf is just the starting point. LEGOLAND Discovery Centre and SEA LIFE Manchester are both at the Trafford Centre, and Chill Factore, with its real indoor snow slope, is just across the way. You could easily build a whole day around these, especially if you're looking for something that works rain or shine.

Football fans won't be far from Old Trafford, home of Manchester United, while Salford Quays has the Imperial War Museum North and The Lowry arts centre for a bit of culture. It's all within easy reach by car or tram.

For the golf itself, a bit of strategy helps. Take a second to look at the slopes before you putt and use the walls for angles. Gentle and steady wins most holes. With little ones, agree on a maximum number of shots per hole so nobody gets stuck, and let the youngest have the odd bonus go if things get tense.
Busy groups will find it easy to organise too, with plenty of places to eat afterwards. Add a hot chocolate or an ice cream for the winner, and the gloating can last all the way home.
